opmech-three-options: Section 1, p.3: the authors list options (i) to (iii) and say they focus on (iii). Scope as the paper states it.
opmech-four-identities: Abstract and Section 2, p.11: the paper names the four identities its own course relies on. Verified in both places; this is its own course toolset.
opmech-sho-no-diffeq: Section 2, p.9-11, Eqs. (27)-(41): the paper's own derivation uses commutators, the Hadamard lemma and a Gaussian normalization only. The quote states what its own derivation uses. Not a theorem; scope of its own method.
opmech-no-standard-assessment: Section 3, p.12: the authors state they cannot use existing measurement assessment instruments, and why. A limit on their own evaluation.
opmech-measurement-destructive-teaching: Section 3, p.12: the authors state how their course treats measurement and why. Its own course design.
opmech-delivery-format: Section 4, p.13: edX remote or in-person flipped; the only difference is in-person instructors. Its own delivery.
opmech-nsf-key-concepts-basis: Section 1, p.3 and Section 4, p.13: the learning goals were based on the nine NSF workshop core principles. Its own course design basis.
opmech-course-four-parts: Section 4, p.14: the quote is verbatim and the next paragraph describes the four parts. Its own course structure.
opmech-abstraction-timing: Conclusions (Section 5 in the text), p.16: abstraction is introduced after a conceptual unit of about 30% of class time. Its own course organization. Passage read in context.
opmech-linear-algebra-caveat: Conclusions, p.17: the authors state their students would benefit from some linear algebra before follow-on quantum computation classes. A caveat the paper states about its own course preparation.
lles-definition: Section II C, p.4: the paper defines its own method LLES as LL plus ES gradient estimation. The quote is the definition and the section opens with it.
lles-bp-not-guaranteed-avoided: Section II C, p.4: the paper states that its indirect parameter correlation does not guarantee that barren plateaus are avoided. A limit on its own method, in the paper's words. result_type 'claim' is fine for a stated limit.
lles-gs-setup-hamiltonian: Section III, p.5 (page rendered): Eq. (18) is the tensor product over n qubits of Pauli Z (the text layer loses the symbol; the render shows it). The paper also states its primary aim is the optimizer, not ground state estimation or QNNs in depth. Setup and scope as the paper states them.
lles-gs-hyperparameter-grid: Section III A, p.5: three learning rates and three sigma values stated. Its own experiment grid.
lles-gs-t-equals-2: Section III A, p.5-6: T = 2 chosen, with the authors' stated reason, and 'in theory any value of T could be employed'. The choice is setup; the reason is the authors' own, stated as theirs.
lles-gs-runs-and-circuit: Section III A, p.5: 8 qubits and L = 8, five runs per configuration, PyTorch. All stated by the paper as its own setup.
lles-qnn-setup: Section III B, p.7: encoding layer, eight hidden layers of Ry then CNOT, last-qubit measurement with O = |0><0|, PyTorch MSE loss, test data for accuracy. All in the passage.
lles-simulation-limit: Section IV, p.9: the authors call this 'a limitation related to the scalability of the proposed method'. The first clause is a field statement, but the paper frames it as its own limit. Stated limit.
lles-appendix-b-noise-setup: Appendix B, p.10-11: correlated amplitude damping noise, parameter lambda in (0,1), sigma = pi/24 used for all noise runs. Its own setup.
lles-appendix-c-setup: Appendix C, p.15: MNIST digits 0, 1, 2; 3000 training and 300 test examples; 10 qubits, L = 15; amplitude encoding. All stated.
lles-scalability-open: Section IV, p.9: the authors state a scalability limitation and that scalability remains an open question. Verified in context.
lles-tasks-setup: Section IV, p.9: the conclusion states the two tasks, and the closing paragraph states Appendices B (noisy circuit) and C (multiclass classification). The widened value matches both quotes. Setup, not a result.
qai-challenges-not-technical: Section 5, p.4: the authors state they focus less on quantum-technical challenges and more on changes to development methods. Scope as the paper states it.
qai-survey-selection: Section 4, p.3: the authors state they surveyed QAI algorithms, present a selection (Table 1), and roughly identified four areas of application. The paper gives no search protocol; the value claims none.
qai-ml-pipeline-definition: Section 2, p.1-2: the paper states what the machine learning pipeline is (a process model of temporal dependences between the creation of artifacts) and uses it for Table 1 and the challenges. The model comes from the authors' ref [22]; the value says 'introduced earlier', so it claims only what this paper says of it.
qai-scope-not-completeness: Section 6, p.5: the authors state the four challenges stand 'without any claim to completeness'. Scope of their own list.
gacon-mclachlan-linear-system: Section II, p.2, Eqs. (3)-(4): the paper defines g as the real part of the QGT and b as the evolution gradient, in the linear system it builds on. The McLachlan principle itself is from ref [17], but the value claims only the paper's own definitions of g and b.
gacon-dual-formulation: Section II A, p.3 (page rendered), Eqs. (7)-(10): the paper defines its own dual formulation and loss, and states the (delta tau)^-2 factor is dropped in practice. Its own algorithm.
gacon-fidelity-method-choice: Section II B, p.4: the paper states its own method choices (parameter-shift gradients and compute-uncompute fidelity) and the reason. Setup.
gacon-global-zero-projector-limit: Section II B, p.4: the authors state the compute-uncompute method may become unsuitable at large qubit counts because it measures the global zero projector (Section II D repeats the point). A limit of their chosen method.
gacon-local-optimizer-needed: Appendix C, p.13: the authors state the infidelity is bounded while the linear term is unbounded, so the minimum near zero is not the global one, and a local optimizer is crucial. A caveat they state on their own method, shown in Fig. 7(a). The true type is a stated limit on the method.
gacon-delta-tau-upper-limit: Appendix C, p.14, Eqs. (C1)-(C2): derived in the paper. The stationary condition plus the parameter-shift bound of [-1/2, 1/2] on the fidelity gradient (a standard tool) gives the range. The conditions (unique parameters, Pauli rotation gates) are carried in the value, and 'necessary, not sufficient' is stated. Borderline: the parameter-shift rule is cited to ref [34] and treated here as a standard tool.
gacon-gd-setup: Section III A, p.6: learning rate 0.1, delta tau 0.01, 100 then 10 steps, and the 'partially heuristic' remark are all stated.
gacon-heisenberg-setup: Section III and III A, p.5-6, Eq. (15): the 12-qubit circle, J = 1/4, g = -1 and Qiskit simulation are all stated.
gacon-bounds-can-be-tight: Section II E, p.5 and III C, p.7: the authors state the bounds can be tight but are not tight in practice, with measured scaling d^3.56 and d^2.29 against the bounds d^5 and d^4. A caveat on their own bounds, in their words. The first clause is asserted, not shown for every component (Appendix D finds the bound on the update norm loose); the value claims no more than the paper says.
gacon-sample-complexity-setup: Section III C, p.7: varying spins, r = ceil(log2 n) repetitions plus a final layer, the mean accuracy I_B <= 0.1 over 5 experiments, and the stated fidelity 0.995 (check: Bures distance 0.1 gives overlap 0.995). Its own setup.
gacon-qmetts-setup: Section III D, p.8: 6-spin chain, J = 1/4, g = -1, alternating X and Y bases, 1024 measurements per basis per energy sample. All stated.
gacon-realtime-setup: Section IV A, p.9: 4 spins, J = 1/4, g = -1, alternating Pauli-X and Pauli-Y layers with ZZ gates, r = 3, T = 2, step T/100. All stated.
gacon-optimizer-limit: Section V, p.10: the authors state they used standard gradient descent with a fixed learning rate, and that a suitable termination criterion for noisy evaluations remains a possible improvement (Section III A and Appendix E 2 say the same). A limit on their own experiments. The expected gain from better optimizers is their expectation, not claimed as a result.
gacon-runtime-assumptions: Appendix A, p.12: the paper states the assumptions of its own runtime estimate (classical overhead neglected, ibm peekskill Falcon gate times, t_reset = 2 microseconds) and that the reset time dominates for the considered shallow circuits. Setup of its own model.
gacon-ansatz-parameter-count: Appendix E 1, p.18-19, Fig. 10: the paper defines its own ansatz (RY and RZ per qubit per layer, r repetitions plus a final layer) and counts 2n(r+1) parameters. A count from its own definition.
gacon-noise-open-questions: Section V, p.10: the authors state that how accurately the error bounds can be evaluated with shot noise remains open, and that accurately measuring the fidelity with hardware noise remains challenging. Limits on their own method.

theory_low.opmech-sho-three-ways: Section 2: only the matrix and operator derivations are given. The Frobenius route is sketched, and the text says 'We won't go through these details any further' (p.4). The matrix derivation rests on Heisenberg postulates. The quote 'the standard result' attaches to the matrix derivation only. The value overstates: three full solutions are not in the paper.
theory_low.opmech-singular-factorization-odd: Section 2, p.8: the 3/2 hbar omega ground energy of the singular factorization is derived. The odd-parity claim is not proved: the text says the states match odd-index nonsingular states 'This can be verified directly by constructing the states, but we do not do so here.' Weaker half decides.
theory_low.opmech-rodrigues-wavefunctions: Section 2, p.6: the general claim cites refs 12 and 13 (ref 13 is 'in preparation'). The paper carries the construction through for the simple harmonic oscillator only (Eqs. 29-41). The value is general, so it rests on citation.
theory_low.lles-parameter-shift-cost: textbook, stated not proved (F129). Introduction, p.2: two executions per parameter is read off Eq. (1), the parameter shift rule, which the paper cites to refs 25 and 26. It is a statement of the cited rule's cost, not a definition and not a result the paper proves. The reader's basis 'definition' does not fit.
theory_low.lles-ll-cost-2pt: Section II A, p.3: the 2pT count is argued in prose (T gradient computations at 2p executions each, 'it is evident'). No proposition or proof. A cost argued informally is not a proved result.
theory_low.lles-es-sample-count: Section II B, p.4: lambda = 4 + 3 log(p) is the standard NES sample-count default taken from the literature (Eq. 14, ref 33), and the logarithmic scaling is asserted as 'evident'. Informal argument, not a proof. The count of circuit executions also needs two evaluations per sample (Eq. 15), which the sentence omits.
theory_low.lles-table-costs: Table I, p.5 (rendered and read): the formulas are stated, with no derivation beyond the informal arguments in Sections II A and II B. Analytic cost claims argued informally are not a proved result.
theory_low.gacon-varqte-circuit-scaling: textbook, stated not proved (F129). Introduction, p.1-2: the O(d^2) and O(d) circuit counts for the QGT and gradients are stated in one sentence, with no derivation. The paper does not define or prove them; they are background on the baseline method.
theory_low.gacon-dual-per-step-cost: Section II A, p.3: an informal cost accounting (O(d) for b times the number of iterations, against O(d^2)). The paper says the condition holds 'as we show in the following sections', that is, by simulation. No proposition and no proof.
theory_low.gacon-circuit-counts: Section III B, p.7, Eqs. (17)-(18): the circuit-count formulas are stated without derivation, and the count for the QGT (d(d+5)/2 + Pd) is not worked out. A count stated, not proved.
theory_low.gacon-time-perturbation-tradeoff: Section II B, p.4: the tradeoff is argued in prose. The cubic error scaling of the infidelity approximation rests on the metric expansion of Eq. (8) and ref [33]. The example in Appendix C illustrates it for one model. Not a proposition with a proof. Section IV B later says the derivative error scales linearly in delta tau.
theory_low.gacon-local-convexity: Section II C, p.4: a one-line assertion with no proof. The stated Hessian g/2 does not match the paper's own Eqs. (8) and (10): with 1 - F = dtheta^T g dtheta, the Hessian of (1 - F)/2 is g, not g/2. The positive semi-definite conclusion would stand either way. The value repeats the stated g/2.
theory_low.gacon-sample-bound-varqte: Section II E, p.5, Eq. (13), derivation in Appendix D (D2)-(D17): the derivation uses Latala's theorem (ref [51], a specific other paper's result) as a step, takes the Poisson-binomial moment bound 'analogous to Ref. [60]', and uses Taylor and Neumann-series approximations with error terms dropped. The result is an O() bound with these steps, not a self-contained proof.
theory_low.gacon-sample-bound-dualqte: Section II E, p.5, Eq. (14), derivation in Appendix D 2: it reuses the Appendix D 1 variance bounds and the lambda_max bound that rests on the QGT-Hessian identity of ref [40]. The text says 'we expect a reduction of a factor d' and asserts the bound ('we can show'). The O() steps are approximations. Not a self-contained proof.
theory_low.gacon-error-bound-loss-link: Section IV B, p.9: the model error rate (Eq. 19) and its integral bound on the Bures distance come from ref [50] ('can be expressed as [50]'). The proportionality to the loss rests on the approximate rewrite with O(delta tau) terms. 'Not possible in p-VQD' is a comparison claim. A cited result plus an informal derivation.
theory_low.gacon-error-bound-delta-tau-scaling: Section IV B, p.9: the linear-in-delta-tau scaling rests on the cubic error term of the infidelity approximation taken from ref [33]. The Euler integration error O(dt + T delta tau) is stated without derivation.
theory_low.gacon-runtime-estimate-claim: Section I, p.2, Fig. 1 and Appendix A: a runtime estimate from a model with assumed IBM Falcon gate times and a 2 microsecond reset, applied to simulated measurement counts. A modeled estimate, not a proved result or a hardware measurement.
theory_low.gacon-fig1-runtime-read: A value read from Figure 1 (page 1 rendered), never HIGH on the figure alone. The reading is also off in places: VarQITE crosses the 1 week line near 200 parameters, but it reaches the 1 year line near 590 parameters and sits near 1.5e4 hours at 700; DualQITE is near the 1 day line (about 25 hours) at 200 parameters, not 30. DualQITE at 700 parameters is near 400 hours.
theory_low.gacon-qng-connection: Appendix B, p.12: 'VarQITE is inherently connected to QNG' is credited to ref [33]. The coincidence of the Euler-integrated update with the QNG step is a comparison of two displayed update rules, not stated as a proposition with a proof. Graded by the weaker.
theory_low.gacon-max-eigenvalue-bound: Appendix D 1 a, p.16: the step uses g_ij = -1/2 d_i d_j F, taken from ref [40] (Gacon et al. 2021), to bound each entry by 1/4 before Gershgorin's theorem. Gershgorin is a standard tool, but the entry identity is a specific cited result. The value also omits the resulting bound lambda_max <= d/4. Borderline.

requote.gacon-qgt-free-method: regraded LOW at the team lead's decision: Abstract, p.1: two claims. 'We propose a dual formulation that circumvents the explicit evaluation of the QGT' is the paper's own scope and definition. 'Quickly become infeasible for relevant system sizes' is the authors' motivating claim, supported only by their modeled runtime (Fig. 1, Appendix A) with stated hardware assumptions; 'relevant system sizes' is not defined. Graded by the weaker. Team lead decides: the second clause is not settled by the paper itself.; team lead, 2026-11-04, Sprint 15 Manual Validation Q1 option 1 (all 36 as proposed)
